title: An uncomplicated method for growing nano-quasicrystalline structures in the AlCuFeB quaternary alloy system: A short-time milling
author: Amini, Rahimipour, et al.

steps.title: Prepare elemental powder mixture
steps.instruction: Weigh high‑purity elemental powders—Al (99 %), Cu (99.7 %), Fe (99.5 %), B (99.9 %)—with average particle size <200 µm to obtain the nominal composition Al59Cu25.5Fe12.5B3 (at %). Perform mixing in a glove box under high‑purified argon to avoid oxidation.

steps.title: Load powders and balls into milling vial
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 g of the mixed powders into a 500 mL hardened‑steel vial together with thirteen 20 mm‑diameter hardened‑steel balls, giving a ball‑to‑powder weight ratio of 45 : 1.

steps.title: Add stearic acid surfactant
steps.instruction: Introduce 1 wt % stearic acid to the vial as a process‑control agent to reduce cold welding and adhesion of the powders to the balls and vial walls.

steps.title: Set up milling parameters and start milling
steps.instruction: Place the sealed vial in a Retsch PM 400 high‑energy planetary ball mill, purge with high‑purified dry argon, and run the mill at 600 rpm under the same argon atmosphere.

steps.title: Perform periodic milling interruptions and reverse rotation
steps.instruction: Every 0.5 h stop the mill, allow the vial to cool to avoid overheating, then reverse the rotation direction before restarting. Continue this cycle until a total milling time of 0.5–3 h is reached (QC phase forms within this interval, after which β‑Al(Cu,Fe) may appear).

steps.title: Sample milled powder for analysis
steps.instruction: At selected milling times, open the vial in an isolated glove box and withdraw approximately 1 g of powder for subsequent characterisation.

steps.title: Optional isothermal annealing of milled powders
steps.instruction: Place the as‑milled powders in a furnace under flowing high‑purified argon and anneal at the predetermined temperature(s) for 4 h.

steps.title: Consolidate powders via cold isostatic pressing
steps.instruction: Load the milled (or annealed) powders into a cylindrical elastomeric mold to form 30 mm‑diameter green compacts, then press in a KJYc300 CIP apparatus at 400 MPa, room temperature, for a soaking time of 5 min.

steps.title: Characterize crystal structure by X‑ray diffraction
steps.instruction: Measure XRD patterns on a PHILIPS‑PW 3710 diffractometer (Cu Kα, λ = 1.54 Å) at 40 kV and 30 mA, scanning 2θ = 20°–70° with step size 0.01° and step time 0.6 s. Analyse data with PANalytical HighScore and MAUD software.

steps.title: Examine microstructure with FESEM and EDS
steps.instruction: Observe morphology and elemental distribution using a TESCAN‑MIRA3 field‑emission SEM equipped with EDS, operating at 5 kV. Perform both point and mapping analyses at the same voltage.

steps.title: Obtain electron diffraction via HRTEM
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑resolution TEM images and electron diffraction patterns of the 1 h milled powders on a Tecni G HRTEM operating at 200 kV.

steps.title: Observe bulk microstructure with optical microscopy
steps.instruction: Inspect the CIP‑consolidated specimens using an Olympus PME3 optical microscope and record images with Axio Vision image‑analysis software.

steps.title: Measure particle size distribution by SLS
steps.instruction: Determine the size distribution of the as‑milled AlCuFeB powders with static light scattering using a Fritsch Particle Size Analysette 22 (laser particle sizer).

steps.title: Determine elemental composition by ICP‑AES
steps.instruction: Analyze the approximate composition (including boron) of the as‑milled powders with a PerkinElmer SCIEX ELAN DRC‑2 inductively coupled plasma‑atomic emission spectrometer.

steps.title: Assess thermal behavior with DTA/TGA
steps.instruction: Run differential thermal analysis and thermogravimetric analysis simultaneously on a BAHR‑STA 503 at a heating rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ under high‑purified argon flowing at 300 cm³ min⁻¹. Identify phases formed during DTA by subsequent XRD.

steps.title: Measure Vickers microhardness
steps.instruction: Perform Vickers hardness tests on consolidated samples using an Akashi MVK‑H1 device with loads of 10–50 g and a dwell time of 15 s. Record at least 10 indentations per sample, calculate the mean value excluding the minimum and maximum readings.

steps.title: Determine green density by Archimedes method
steps.instruction: Measure the green density of each ball‑milled powder compact via the Archimedes technique using de‑ionized water as the immersion medium.

steps.title: Measure electrical resistivity with four‑point probe
steps.instruction: Assess the room‑temperature electrical resistivity of the consolidated as‑milled and heat‑treated samples using a standard four‑point probe DC method, reporting the mean of ten measurements.

steps.title: Record UV‑Vis‑NIR reflectance spectra
steps.instruction: Collect diffuse reflectance spectra of the CIP‑fabricated samples on a PerkinElmer Lambda 25 UV/VIS spectrometer over 250–1000 nm, using a fiber‑optic reflection probe R200‑7‑SR positioned ~4 mm from the sample to minimise scattering losses.
